兵者，守國之備。 孔子曰：「以不教民戰，是謂棄之。 」兵，凶事，不可空設，因蒐狩而習之。 而凡師出曰治兵，入曰振旅，皆戰陳之事，辨鼓鐸鐲鐃之用，以教坐作進退疾徐疏數之節，遂以蒐田。 獻禽以祭社。 仲夏教茇舍，如振旅之陳，遂以苗田，如蒐之法。 獻禽以享礿。 仲秋教治兵，如振旅之陳，遂以獮田，如蒐之法。 致禽以祀方。 仲冬教大閱，遂以狩田。 獻禽以享蒸。 蒐者，蒐索取其不孕者也。 苗者，為苗除害而已。 獮者，殺也。 從秋氣所殺多也。 狩者，冬物畢成，獲則取之，無所擇也。
Arms are what guard the state. Confucius said: "To lead the people to war without teaching them is to throw them away. War is an inauspicious affair and cannot be maintained in idleness; it is practiced through hunts and reviews. When an army sets out it is called ordering the troops; when it enters camp, marshaling the columns. Both concern battle formations: distinguishing the use of drums, bells, gongs, and cymbals, and teaching the cadences of sitting, rising, advancing, retreating, speed, spacing, and density—and so the hunt field serves as the school. The captured game is offered in sacrifice to the soil god. In midsummer troops are taught to set camp, arrayed as in marshaling the columns, then the seedling hunt is held by the same methods as the great hunt. The captured game is offered in the yue sacrifice. In mid-autumn troops are taught to order the ranks, arrayed as in marshaling the columns, then the extermination hunt is held by the same methods as the great hunt. The captured game is presented in sacrifice at the directional altar. In mid-winter the great review is taught, then the winter hunt is held. The captured game is offered in the winter sacrifice. The great hunt gathers game but takes only those not bearing young. The seedling hunt is only for clearing pests from the seedlings. The extermination hunt means killing. It follows the autumn qi, the season when much is killed. The winter hunt comes when winter's creatures are fully grown: what is caught is taken, with no special selection.
92
漢儀，立秋日，郊禮畢，始揚威武，斬牲於郊，以薦陵廟，名曰貙劉。 其儀，乘輿御戎路，白馬朱鬣，躬執弩射牲。 太宰令以獲車送陵廟。 於是乘輿還宮，遣使以束帛賜武官，肄孫、吳兵法戰陳之儀，率以為常。 至獻帝建安二十一年，魏國有司奏：「古四時講武，皆於農隙。 漢西京承秦制，三時不講，唯十月都試。 今兵革未偃，士民素習，可無四時講武。 但以立秋擇吉日大朝車騎，號曰治兵。 上合禮名，下承漢制。 」奏可。 是冬，治兵。 魏王親金鼓以令進退。
In Han ritual, on Beginning of Autumn, after the suburban sacrifice was complete, martial display was first raised. A victim was beheaded in the suburbs and offered to the imperial tombs—the rite was called the Leopard Slaying. In the rite the emperor rode the war chariot with a white horse and red mane and personally shot the victim with a crossbow. The Grand Steward ordered the capture cart to carry it to the imperial tombs. The emperor then returned to the palace and sent envoys to bestow silk on military officers. The arts of Sun and Wu and the formations of battle were drilled, and this became the regular custom. In the twenty-first year of Jian'an under Emperor Xian, Wei's relevant offices memorialized: "In antiquity military instruction was given in all four seasons, always during the gaps in farm work. The Western Capital of Han followed Qin practice: in three seasons there was no instruction—only in the tenth month was the capital review held. Now arms are not yet laid aside, and officers and people are already well trained—four-season instruction is unnecessary. But on Beginning of Autumn an auspicious day should be chosen for the great assembly of chariots and horsemen, called ordering the troops. Above it matches the ritual name; below it continues Han practice. The memorial was approved. That winter the troops were ordered. The King of Wei personally beat gongs and drums to command advance and retreat.
93
延康元年，魏文帝為魏王，是年六月立秋，治兵于東郊，公卿相儀。 王御華蓋，親令金鼓之節。
In the first year of Yankang, Cao Pi was King of Wei. That sixth month, at Beginning of Autumn, troops were ordered in the eastern suburb, with princes and ministers assisting in the rite. The king rode beneath the flowered canopy and personally commanded the cadences of gongs and drums.
94
明帝太和元年十月，治兵于東郊。
In the tenth month of the first year of Taihe under Emperor Ming, troops were ordered in the eastern suburb.

晉武帝泰始四年、九年、咸寧元年、太康四年、六年冬，皆自臨宣武觀，大習眾軍。 然不自令進退也。 自惠帝以後，其禮遂廢。
In the fourth and ninth years of Taishi, the first year of Xianning, and the fourth and sixth years of Taikang under Jin Emperor Wu—all in winter—the emperor personally visited the Xuanwu Viewing Stand and conducted the great review of the assembled armies. Yet he did not personally command advance and retreat. From Emperor Hui onward, the rite was abandoned.

元帝太興四年，詔左右衞及諸營教習，依大習儀作雁羽仗。 成帝咸和中，詔內外諸軍戲兵於南郊之場，故其地因名鬭場。 自後蕃鎮桓、庾諸方伯，往往閱習，然朝廷無事焉。
In the fourth year of Daxing under Emperor Yuan, an edict ordered the Left and Right Guards and the various camps to practice drill, making goose-wing arms according to the great review rite. In the Xianhe era under Emperor Cheng, an edict ordered the inner and outer armies to perform mock battle on the field south of the southern suburb—hence the place was named the Fighting Ground. Afterward frontier commanders such as Huan and Yu often held reviews, yet the court itself did nothing.

太祖在位，依故事肄習眾軍，兼用漢、魏之禮。 其後以時講武於宣武堂。 元嘉二十五年閏二月，大蒐於宣武場，主司奉詔列奏申攝，克日校獵，百官備辦。 設行宮殿便坐武帳於幕府山南岡。 設王公百官便坐幔省如常儀，設南北左右四行旌門。 建獲旗以表獲車。 殿中郎一人典獲車。 主者二人收禽。 吏二十四人配獲車。 備獲車十二兩。 校獵之官著袴褶。 有帶武冠者。 脫冠者上纓。 二品以上擁刀，備槊、麾幡，三品以下帶刀。 皆騎乘。 將領部曲先獵一日，遣屯布圍。 領軍將軍一人督右甄； 護軍一人督左甄； 大司馬一人居中，董正諸軍，悉受節度。 殿中郎率獲車部曲，在司馬之後。 尚書僕射、都官尚書、五兵尚書、左右丞、都官諸曹郎、都令史、都官諸曹令史幹、蘭臺治書侍御史令史、諸曹令史幹，督攝糾司，校獵非違。 至日，會於宣武場，列為重圍。 設留守填街位於雲龍門外內官道北，外官道南，以西為上。 設從官位於雲龍門內大官階北，小官階南，以西為上。 設先置官位於行止車門外內官道西，外官道東，以北為上。 設先置官還位於廣莫門外道之東西，以南為上。 校獵日平旦，正直侍中奏嚴。 上水一刻，奏：「搥一鼓。 」為一嚴。 上水二刻，奏：「搥二鼓。 」為再嚴。 殿中侍御史奏開東中華雲龍門，引仗為小駕鹵簿。 百官非校獵之官，著朱服，集列廣莫門外。 應還省者還省。 留守填街後部從官就位； 前部從官依鹵簿； 先置官先行。 上水三刻，奏：「搥三鼓。 」為三嚴。 上水四刻，奏：「外辦。 」正次直侍中、散騎常侍、給事黃門侍郎、軍校劍履進夾上閤。 正直侍郎負璽，通事令史帶龜印中書之印。 上水五刻，皇帝出。 著黑介幘單衣，乘輦。 正直侍中負璽陪乘，不帶劍。 殿中侍御史督攝黃麾以內。 次直侍中、次直黃門侍郎護駕在前。 又次直侍中佩信璽、行璽，與正直黃門侍郎從護駕在後。 不鳴鼓角，不得諠譁，以次引出，警蹕如常儀。 車駕出，騶讚，陛者再拜。 皇太子入守。 車駕將至，威儀唱：「引先置前部從官就位。 」再拜。 車駕至行殿前回輦，正直侍中跪奏：「降輦。 」次直侍中稱制曰：「可。 」正直侍中俛伏起。 皇帝降輦登御坐，侍臣升殿。 直衞靸戟虎賁，旄頭文衣，鶡尾，以次列階。 正直侍中奏：「解嚴。 」先置從駕百官還便坐幔省。
While Emperor Wen was on the throne, he drilled the assembled armies according to precedent, combining Han and Wei rites. Afterward military instruction was given at the Xuanwu Hall according to the season. In the intercalary second month of the twenty-fifth year of Yuanjia a great hunt was held at the Xuanwu Field. The presiding office, following the edict, submitted the schedule, fixed the day for the military hunt, and all officials made ready. A traveling palace hall with a military tent for informal seating was set up on the southern hill of the headquarters mountain. Informal tents for princes, dukes, and officials were set up according to the usual rite, with four rows of banner gates to north, south, left, and right. Capture banners were erected to mark the capture carts. One Palace Gentleman served as master of the capture carts. Two stewards collected the game. Twenty-four clerks were assigned to the capture carts. Twelve capture carts were prepared. Officers of the military hunt wore trousers and short jackets. Those wearing the martial cap with chin strap kept it on. Those removing the cap put on the tassel headband. Those of the second rank and above carried swords at the side and were equipped with spears and command banners; those of the third rank and below wore swords at the belt. All rode on horseback. The generals' units hunted one day in advance, sending detachments to deploy the encirclement. One General Who Leads the Army supervised the right wing; one Protector General supervised the left wing; and one Grand Marshal stood at the center, directing all armies, all under his command. The Palace Gentleman led the capture-cart units behind the Marshal. The Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Director of Judgments, Director of the Five Armies, Left and Right Vice Directors, bureau gentlemen, chief clerks, and clerks of the Judgments, Secretariat, and Censorate offices supervised and corrected violations at the hunt. On the appointed day they assembled at the Xuanwu Field and formed a double encirclement. Garrison positions filling the streets were set north of the inner official road and south of the outer official road outside the Cloud Dragon Gate, with west as the place of honor. Positions for attendant officials were set north of the great official steps and south of the lesser official steps inside the Cloud Dragon Gate, with west as the place of honor. Positions for officials placed in advance were set west of the inner official road and east of the outer official road outside the Traveling Halt Gate, with north as the place of honor. Return positions for officials placed in advance were set east and west along the road outside the Broad Mo Gate, with south as the place of honor. On the day of the military hunt, at dawn the duty Attendant-in-Ordinary announced the first martial alert. One quarter before the water clock's upper mark came the announcement: "Strike one drum. This was the first alert. Two quarters before the upper mark came: "Strike two drums. This was the second alert. The Palace Attendant announced the opening of the East Central Flower Cloud Dragon Gate and led out the guard as the small imperial escort. Officials not taking part in the hunt, wearing vermilion robes, assembled outside the Broad Mo Gate. Those who should return to their offices did so. The garrison filling the streets and the rear attendant officials took their positions; the front attendant officials followed the imperial escort; and the officials placed in advance went ahead. Three quarters before the upper mark came: "Strike three drums. This was the third alert. Four quarters before the upper mark came: "The outer preparations are complete. The duty Attendant-in-Ordinary, Regular Palace Attendant, Yellow Gate Attendant-in-Ordinary, and military officers with swords and shoes advanced on either side of the upper gate. The duty Vice Attendant carried the imperial seal; the Master of Protocol Clerk carried the tortoise seal of the Secretariat—the seal of the Masters of Writing. Five quarters before the upper mark, the emperor emerged. He wore a black kerchief cap and unlined robe and rode in the palanquin. The duty Attendant-in-Ordinary carried the seal and rode with him, without sword. The Palace Attendant supervised those within the yellow banner. The alternate Attendant-in-Ordinary and alternate Yellow Gate Attendant-in-Ordinary escorted in front. Again the alternate Attendant-in-Ordinary wore the trust seal and traveling seal and, with the duty Yellow Gate Attendant-in-Ordinary, followed escorting from behind. Drums and horns were not sounded; no clamor was permitted; they were led out in order with the usual clearing of the way. When the imperial carriage emerged, the outriders announced; those on the steps bowed twice. The crown prince entered to stand guard. As the imperial carriage was about to arrive, the guard of honor called: "Lead the front attendant officials placed in advance to their positions. They bowed twice. When the imperial carriage reached the traveling hall and turned, the duty Attendant-in-Ordinary knelt and announced: "Descend from the palanquin. The alternate Attendant-in-Ordinary proclaimed the command: "It is permitted. The duty Attendant-in-Ordinary bowed low and rose. The emperor descended from the palanquin and ascended the imperial seat; attendant ministers ascended the hall. The direct guards with halberds drawn from scabbards, tiger guards in plumed-head patterned robes with pheasant-tail feathers, lined the steps in order. The duty Attendant-in-Ordinary announced: "Release martial alert. The officials placed in advance who had escorted the emperor returned to the informal tent offices.
98
帝若躬親射禽，變御戎服，內外從官以及虎賁悉變服，如校獵儀。 靸戟抽鞘，以備武衞。 黃麾內官，從入圍裏。 列置部曲，廣張甄圍，旗鼓相望，銜枚而進。 甄周圍會，督甄令史奔騎號法施令曰：「春禽懷孕，蒐而不射； 鳥獸之肉不登於俎，不射； 皮革齒牙骨角毛羽不登於器，不射。 」甄會。 大司馬鳴鼓蹙圍，眾軍鼓譟警角，至宣武場止。 大司馬屯北旌門； 二甄帥屯左右旌門； 殿中中郎率獲車部曲入次北旌門內之右。 皇帝從南旌門入射禽。 謁者以獲車收載，還陳於獲旗北。 王公以下以次射禽，各送詣獲旗下，付收禽主者。 事畢。 大司馬鳴鼓解圍復屯，殿中郎率其屬收禽，以實獲車，充庖厨。 列言統曹正厨，置尊酒俎肉于中逵，以犒饗校獵眾軍。 至晡，正直侍中量宜奏嚴，從官還著朱服，靸戟復鞘。 再嚴，先置官先還。 三嚴後二刻，正直侍中奏：「外辦。 」皇帝著黑介幘單衣。 正次直侍中、散騎常侍、給事黃門侍郎、軍校進夾御坐。 正直侍中跪奏：「還宮。 」次直侍中稱制曰：「可。 」正直侍中俛伏起。 乘輿登輦還，衞從如常儀。 大司馬鳴鼓散屯，以次就舍。 車駕將至，威儀唱：「引留守填街先置前部從官就位。 」再拜。 車駕至殿前回輦，正直侍中跪奏：「降輦。 」次直侍中稱制曰：「可。 」正直侍中俛伏起。 乘輿降入。 正直次直侍中、散騎常侍、給事黃門侍郎、散騎侍郎、軍校從至閤，亦如常儀。 正直侍中奏：「解嚴。 」內外百官拜表問訊如常儀，訖，罷。
If the emperor personally shot game, he changed to military dress; inner and outer attendants and the tiger guards all changed dress according to the military hunt rite. Halberds were drawn from scabbards to serve as military guard. Inner officials within the yellow banner followed into the encirclement. Units were deployed in array; the wing encirclement was spread wide; flags and drums faced one another; they advanced with gags in their mouths. When the wings closed the encirclement, the wing command clerks galloped and shouted the legal command: "In spring, birds and beasts with young are gathered but not shot; the flesh of birds and beasts not destined for the sacrificial stand—do not shoot; hide, teeth, bone, horn, feather, and down not destined for use—do not shoot. The wings closed. The Grand Marshal sounded the drum to tighten the encirclement; the assembled armies beat drums, shouted, and sounded warning horns until they halted at the Xuanwu Field. The Grand Marshal encamped at the northern banner gate; the two wing commanders encamped at the left and right banner gates; and the Palace Central Gentleman led the capture-cart units to enter and take position to the right inside the northern banner gate. The emperor entered through the southern banner gate to shoot game. Ushers used the capture carts to collect and load the game, then returned and displayed it north of the capture banners. Princes, dukes, and those below shot game in turn, each sending it to the capture banners and delivering it to the stewards who collected the game. The affair was finished. The Grand Marshal sounded the drum to release the encirclement and encamped again; the Palace Gentleman led his subordinates to collect game, filling the capture carts to supply the kitchens. A report was sent to the chief kitchen of the unified bureau; wine vessels and sacrificial meat were placed at the central crossroads to feast the assembled armies of the hunt. At the hour of shen the duty Attendant-in-Ordinary judged the occasion and announced martial alert; attendant officials returned to vermilion robes and halberds were resheathed. At the second alert the officials placed in advance returned first. Two quarters after the third alert the duty Attendant-in-Ordinary announced: "The outer preparations are complete. The emperor wore a black kerchief cap and unlined robe. The duty Attendant-in-Ordinary, Regular Palace Attendant, Yellow Gate Attendant-in-Ordinary, and military officers advanced on either side of the imperial seat. The duty Attendant-in-Ordinary knelt and announced: "Return to the palace. The alternate Attendant-in-Ordinary proclaimed the command: "It is permitted. The duty Attendant-in-Ordinary bowed low and rose. The imperial carriage mounted the palanquin and returned; the guard and escort followed the usual rite. The Grand Marshal sounded the drum to disperse the encampments; each returned to quarters in order. As the imperial carriage was about to arrive, the guard of honor called: "Lead the garrison filling the streets and the front attendant officials placed in advance to their positions. They bowed twice. When the imperial carriage reached the hall and turned, the duty Attendant-in-Ordinary knelt and announced: "Descend from the palanquin. The alternate Attendant-in-Ordinary proclaimed the command: "It is permitted. The duty Attendant-in-Ordinary bowed low and rose. The imperial carriage descended and entered. The duty and alternate Attendants-in-Ordinary, Regular Palace Attendants, Yellow Gate Attendants-in-Ordinary, Regular Attendants-in-Ordinary, and military officers followed to the gate, likewise according to the usual rite. The duty Attendant-in-Ordinary announced: "Release martial alert. Inner and outer officials submitted memorials of inquiry according to the usual rite; when finished, the rite was dismissed.
